sn43.15:1.1: Nibbāna is the truth since delusion has ceased ([mn140:26.2]()).
sn43.16:1.1: This is a common metaphor, eg. [snp5.18:1.3]().
sn43.17:1.1: For this term and the next, see [dhp36:1](), [thag2.46:2.3]()
sn43.19:1.1: “Undecrepit” (_ajajjara_) doesn’t appear elsewhere in Pali. However, Buddhist Sanskrit texts sometimes use _jarjara_ (“decrepitude”) in definitions of old age in dependent origination (Nidānasaṁyukta 16.15, Pratītyasamutpādavibhaṅgasūtra 15b, Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra 118, Dharmaskandha 16v2).
sn43.20:1.1: “Everlasting” (_dhuva_) is normally a synonym of “permanent” (_nicca_). It is used of Brahmā ([sn6.4:1.4]()), and of Nibbāna at [iti43:4.4]().
sn43.21:1.1: “Not worn out” (_apalokita_) is apparently unique in this sense. “Wearing out” (_paloka_) is a characteristic of conditioned things ([sn35.84:2.3]()).
sn43.22:1.1: Normally _anidassana_ means “invisible” ([dn33:1.10.76]()) or “formless” ([mn21:14.8]()), although it is sometimes interpreted to mean Nibbāna ([dn11:85.18]()). While Nibbāna is, of course, formless and invisible, this is, I believe, the only place _anidassana_ unambiguously refers to Nibbāna.
sn43.30:1.1: This term and the next are commonly used of individuals who have realized Nibbāna ([an6.46:6.5](), [sn51.22:2.2]()).
sn43.35:1.1: Normally a term for the mind developed through love, etc. ([mn21:11.14]()), or for good acts with pleasant outcomes ([an3.23:2.1](), [mn57:9.2]()).
sn43.39:1.1: “Not clinging” (_anālaya_) is part of the standard definition of the third noble truth ([sn56.11:4.7]()).
sn43.40:1.1: [snp5.11:3.2](). | This series of terms is used of the Buddha ([sn42.7]()) or one’s own good deeds ([an3.51:2.4]()).
